question: A previously healthy 8-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of increasing visual loss and deterioration of his hearing and speech over the past 2 months. During this period, he has had difficulty walking, using the stairs, and feeding himself. His teachers have noticed that he has had difficulty concentrating. His grades have worsened and his handwriting has become illegible. His maternal male cousin had similar complaints and died at the age of 6 years. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows hyperpigmented skin and nails and an ataxic gait. His speech is dysarthric. Neurologic examination shows spasticity and decreased muscle strength in all extremities. Deep tendon reflexes are 4+ bilaterally. Plantar reflex shows an extensor response bilaterally. Sensation is decreased in the lower extremities. Fundoscopy shows optic atrophy. There is sensorineural hearing loss bilaterally. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Arylsulfatase A deficiency -> Metachromatic leukodystrophy -> Progressive deterioration of vision, hearing, speech, and motor function -> 90% CHAIN: Metachromatic leukodystrophy -> Hyperpigmented skin and nails -> Ataxic gait -> Dysarthric speech -> Spasticity and decreased muscle strength -> 90% CHAIN: Ataxic gait -> Difficulty walking and using stairs -> 90% CHAIN: Dysarthric speech -> Difficulty feeding oneself -> 90% CHAIN: Spasticity and decreased muscle strength -> Decreased sensation in lower extremities -> 90% CHAIN: Optic atrophy -> Visual loss -> 90% CHAIN: Sensorineural hearing loss -> Hearing loss -> 90% CHAIN: Hyperpigmented skin and nails -> 90% CHAIN: Difficulty concentrating -> Worsened grades and illegible handwriting -> 90% CHAIN: Family history of similar complaints and early death -> Genetic component -> 90%
enhanced_information: The most likely cause of this patient's symptoms is Arylsulfatase A deficiency, leading to Metachromatic leukodystrophy. The symptoms of progressive deterioration of vision, hearing, speech, and motor function, along with hyperpigmented skin and nails, ataxic gait, dysarthric speech, spasticity, decreased muscle strength, optic atrophy, sensorineural hearing loss, and difficulty concentrating, are all consistent with this diagnosis. The evidence paths support the manifestations of hyperpigmentation, ataxic gait, and hearing issues seen in Metachromatic leukodystrophy.
analysis: The core medical principle guiding this case is the recognition of the symptoms and signs consistent with Metachromatic leukodystrophy. The patient's presentation of progressive visual loss, hearing loss, speech deterioration, motor dysfunction, hyperpigmented skin and nails, ataxic gait, dysarthric speech, spasticity, decreased muscle strength, optic atrophy, sensorineural hearing loss, and cognitive decline align with the known manifestations of Arylsulfatase A deficiency. This enzyme deficiency leads to the accumulation of sulfatides in various tissues, causing the observed clinical features.
